description:
chat-server uses match args.remove(key).unwrap_or(Value::Null) { Value::Null => None, v => Some(...) } across 26 sites in space.rs / message.rs / chat.rs / etc., while canonical jmap-mail-server (email.rs) uses match args.remove(key) { None | Some(Value::Null) => None, Some(v) => Some(...) } across 48 sites.

The mail-server idiom is one step cleaner: serde_json::Map::remove already returns Option<Value>, and the absent-vs-null distinction is irrelevant for JMAP optional argument parsing per RFC 8620 §3.4 (both surface as 'argument not supplied'). The chat-server form materializes a synthetic Value::Null intermediate that the immediately-following match then discards.

Engineering basis: this is a canonical-template divergence per workspace AGENTS.md propagation rule. Mail-server has the better shape; chat-server should propagate. The fix is mechanical (s/match args.remove("X").unwrap_or(Value::Null) { Value::Null /match args.remove("X") { None | Some(Value::Null)/, s/v => Some/Some(v) => Some/) and improves readability + removes a no-op allocation step.

Sites: space.rs:343, 356, 607, 619, 626, 631; message.rs and chat.rs similar (grep 'args.remove.*unwrap_or(Value::Null)' for full list — 26 total in chat-server, 0 in mail-server).

Idiomatic Rust would prefer matching directly on the Option<Value> rather than synthesizing a Value::Null inside it. The pattern 'None | Some(Value::Null)' reads as 'absent or explicitly null' which is what the JMAP optional-arg convention actually says.

Canonical-template implication: since mail-server is already correct, the propagation direction is mail → chat (chat changes, mail unchanged). No mail-server work required.
title: 26 sites of args.remove(key).unwrap_or(Value::Null) diverge from canonical mail-server one-fewer-step idiom
